info.title: Useful info
info.subtitle: FAQ about the air quality scale, data sources, and how we generate recommendations.
info.a1: Wispi is a friendly <bold>little wisp who loves helping people</bold>. Wispi keeps an eye on air quality and shares clear, useful information so you can make better decisions for your health and daily life.
info.q2: Where does the air quality data come from?
info.a2: From <bold>OpenWeather’s Air Pollution API</bold>, based on coordinates for your selected location.
info.q3: What is the OpenWeather AQI scale (1–5)?
info.a3: OpenWeather uses a simple 1–5 Air Quality Index <bold>where 1 is the best and 5 is the worst</bold>. While this scale is specific to OpenWeather, it generally aligns with standard international categories for health-based reporting.
info.q4: What does each AQI level mean?
info.a4_1: <bold>1 — Good:</bold> air is clean, enjoy outdoor activities.
info.a4_2: <bold>2 — Fair:</bold> acceptable, minor risk for very sensitive people.
info.a4_4: <bold>4 — Poor:</bold> high risk for sensitive groups, recommended to reduce outdoor activity for all people.
info.q5: Where do the recommendations come from?
info.a5: Recommendations are simple preset messages based on the <bold>United States Environmental Protection Agency</bold> and aligned with OpenWeather AQI scale.
info.q6: Why is knowledge about current air quality important?
info.a6_1: Almost all of the global population is exposed to air pollution levels that exceed the safe guidelines set by the World Health Organization (WHO). The highest levels of exposure are typically found in low- and middle-income countries.
info.a6_2: <bold>Ambient (outdoor) air pollution</bold> comes from sources such as traffic, industry, and wildfires. <bold>Household air pollution</bold> is caused by the burning of fuels for cooking or heating indoors, and it can also contribute to outdoor pollution.
info.a6_3: The combined effects of outdoor and household air pollution are linked to around <bold>7 million premature deaths every year</bold>, increasing the risk of stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer, and acute respiratory infections.
info.a6_4: By staying informed about current air quality conditions, you can take simple but meaningful steps to protect yourself and your loved ones — such as limiting outdoor activity, improving ventilation, or planning exercise and travel more wisely. Awareness helps you make better daily decisions that can improve your overall quality of life.
info.q7: Why can two nearby places show different results?
info.a7: Air quality can vary with traffic, wind, humidity, and local sources. Provider grid resolution and update frequency can also affect values.
info.q8: Are the health tips shown for different air quality levels medical advice?
info.a8: <bold>No.</bold> Provided recommendations are for general informational purposes only and are not a substitute for professional medical advice. If you have a medical condition or feel unwell, always follow the medical professional guidance.
info.q9: Is this service free to use?
info.a9: <bold>Yes.</bold> The service is completely free of charge. All features are available without any fees or subscriptions.
info.q10: How can I report a bug or get in touch?
info.a10: If you notice a bug, have a suggestion, or want to share feedback, feel free to contact me through the <bold>Contacts section</bold>. Your input helps make the service better.
